## Topic: LLM Gateway — Functional Specification

source: documentazione/03-analisi-funzionale/01-llm-gateway.md

The LLM Gateway is the central abstraction layer for multi-provider LLM access. It implements Strategy + Chain of Responsibility patterns for provider routing and fallback.

Provider matrix (as of spec v0.1.0, Feb 9 2026):
  Ollama: local, HTTP REST, port 11434, models Llama 3 / Mistral / Phi-3 / Gemma
  OpenAI: cloud, HTTP REST, models GPT-4o / GPT-4o-mini / GPT-4 Turbo
  Anthropic: cloud, HTTP REST, models Claude 3.5 Sonnet / Claude 3 Opus
  Google: cloud, HTTP REST, models Gemini 1.5 Pro / Gemini 1.5 Flash
  Note: DeepSeek, Mistral, XAI added post-spec (confirmed in PROJECT.md Validated)

Provider selection order:
  1. Explicitly specified in request
  2. Default configured (localmind.llm.default-provider, default: OLLAMA)
  3. First available in fallback chain (default: OLLAMA -> OPENAI -> ANTHROPIC -> GOOGLE)

Fallback triggers: provider timeout, HTTP 5xx, provider disabled in config, rate limit exceeded

Rate limiting: respects HTTP 429 + Retry-After header

Cost tracking: CostTrackingService computes per-request cost (input tokens * price + output tokens * price), persisted via LlmUsageRepository. Metrics aggregated by provider, model, time period.

Usage metrics collected per call: promptTokens, completionTokens, totalTokens, latencyMs, provider, model, estimatedCost

Configuration reference (application-dev.yml):
  localmind.llm.default-provider: OLLAMA
  localmind.llm.ollama.enabled: true, base-url: http://localhost:11434, model: llama3.2, embedding-model: nomic-embed-text, timeout: 120s
  localmind.llm.openai.enabled: false, api-key: ${OPENAI_API_KEY:}, model: gpt-4o-mini, timeout: 60s
  localmind.llm.anthropic.enabled: false, api-key: ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY:}, model: claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, timeout: 60s
  localmind.llm.google.enabled: false, api-key: ${GOOGLE_API_KEY:}, model: gemini-1.5-flash, timeout: 60s
  localmind.llm.retry.max-attempts: 3, backoff-ms: 1000
  localmind.llm.fallback.enabled: true, order: OLLAMA,OPENAI,ANTHROPIC,GOOGLE

Error behavior:
  HTTP 408, 500, 503 -> retry, then fallback
  HTTP 429 -> wait Retry-After, then retry
  HTTP 401, 403 -> error immediately, no retry, no fallback
  All providers exhausted -> HTTP 503 with descriptive message

## Topic: Document Intelligence and RAG Pipeline — Functional Specification

source: documentazione/03-analisi-funzionale/02-document-intelligence-rag.md

Three sub-systems: Ingestion (upload + folder scan) -> Processing (extract, chunk, embed, store) -> Retrieval (semantic search + Q&A).

Ingestion modes:
  Manual upload: POST /api/v1/documents/upload (multipart), max 50MB, returns 202 Accepted
  Folder scanning: configurable paths, recursive option, Spring Batch cron (default: every 15 min), optional real-time WatchService (disabled by default)

Supported formats per functional spec: PDF (Tika), DOCX (Tika), TXT (direct), EML (Tika)
  NOTE: roadmap completion doc lists 9 formats; see INGEST-CONFLICTS.md WARNING "Supported document formats"

Deduplication: SHA-256 hash of file content; skip if hash already in DB (applies to both upload and folder scan)

RAG pipeline (5 phases):
  Phase 1 — Text Extraction: Apache Tika 2.9.2; extracts plain text + metadata (title, author, date, pages)
  Phase 2 — Chunking: ChunkingService custom; default 500 chars, 50 overlap; metadata: documentId, chunkIndex, startOffset, endOffset
  Phase 3 — Embedding: Ollama nomic-embed-text (default); alternatives: text-embedding-3-small (OpenAI), voyage-2 (Anthropic); batch processing
  Phase 4 — Vector Storage: Qdrant collection localmind_documents; gRPC 6334 (primary), HTTP 6333 (fallback); payload includes documentId, filename, chunkIndex, original text
  Phase 5 — Semantic Search: embed query, cosine similarity, top-K=5, threshold=0.7; response includes citations (documentId, filename, chunkIndex, similarityScore)

Document status lifecycle: PENDING -> PROCESSING -> INDEXED / FAILED -> ARCHIVED (FAILED -> PENDING via manual retry)

Folder scan configuration:
  localmind.documents.folders[].path, .recursive, .enabled
  localmind.documents.scan.cron: "0 */15 * * * *"
  localmind.documents.scan.watcher-enabled: false

Knowledge Graph relevance:
  INGEST-01 requires KnowledgeEntity creation when document reaches INDEXED state
  The localmind_documents Qdrant collection must remain separate from localmind_graph_nodes
  The existing DocumentIngestionUseCase interface must be extended (not replaced) to also emit a graph node

## Topic: AI Agents — Functional Specification

source: documentazione/03-analisi-funzionale/03-ai-agents.md

Four predefined specialized agents:

TECH agent: for developers/DevOps/architects; temp 0.2, max 4096 tokens; focus: debug, code review, architecture analysis, documentation generation
BUSINESS agent: for managers/analysts; temp 0.5, max 4096 tokens; focus: reports, executive summaries, data analysis, presentation creation
LEGAL agent: for lawyers/compliance officers; temp 0.1, max 4096 tokens; focus: contract analysis, risk identification, regulatory references, compliance checklists
PERSONAL agent: for students/general users; temp 0.7, max 2048 tokens; focus: simple explanations, writing assistance, translation, organization

Execution pattern: ReAct (Reasoning -> Acting -> Observation -> Response)

Available tools per agent:
  document_search: semantic search via RAG (always available)
  calculator: mathematical operations
  formatter: output formatting
  web_search: web search (future, not yet implemented)

Tool parameters schema: JSON Schema for each tool. Example for document_search:
  { "type": "object", "properties": { "query": { "type": "string" }, "topK": { "type": "integer", "default": 5 } }, "required": ["query"] }

REST API: POST /api/v1/agents/execute
  Request: { agentId: UUID, query: String }
  Response: AgentExecutionResult { response, citations, toolCalls, latencyMs, provider, model, tokenUsage }
  Citations: { documentId, filename, chunkIndex, text, similarityScore }

Architecture:
  Domain: Agent entity, AgentType enum (TECH/BUSINESS/LEGAL/PERSONAL), AgentTool value object, AgentExecutionResult value object, Citation value object
  Port in: AgentExecutionUseCase
  Port out: AgentConfigRepository
  Domain service: AgentService
  Infrastructure: AgentEntity (JPA), JpaAgentRepository, AgentConfigPersistenceAdapter
  API: AgentController (/api/v1/agents), AgentExecutionRequestDto, AgentExecutionResponseDto

Knowledge Graph relevance:
  GraphRAG chat (Phase 7) is a separate feature from the existing agents; it uses a new /api/v1/graph-rag/query endpoint
  Existing agents could in future be extended with a graph_search tool, but this is not in the current roadmap phases

## Topic: n8n Automation Integration — Functional Specification

source: documentazione/03-analisi-funzionale/04-automazioni-n8n.md

Integration model: bidirectional HTTP webhook
  LocalMind -> n8n: events trigger workflow execution via HTTP POST to n8n webhook URL
  n8n -> LocalMind: workflows call LocalMind REST API for operations (ingest, chat, search)

Supported event types (AutomationEvent enum):
  NEW_FILE: new file detected in filesystem; payload: filePath, filename, size, hash
  DOCUMENT_INDEXED: document indexed in RAG; payload: documentId, filename, chunkCount
  DOCUMENT_FAILED: document indexing failed; payload: documentId, filename, error
  SCHEDULED: cron trigger; payload: scheduleName, timestamp
  CHAT_COMPLETED: chat conversation completed; payload: conversationId, provider, tokens
  AGENT_EXECUTED: AI agent executed; payload: agentType, query, latencyMs

Dispatch mechanism:
  1. Internal event occurs in LocalMind
  2. AutomationService receives event
  3. Service queries DB for webhooks registered for that event type
  4. For each registered webhook: WebhookClientPort sends HTTP POST to n8n webhook URL
  5. n8n executes the associated workflow

Webhook entity fields: id (UUID), name, url, eventType (AutomationEvent), enabled, headers (Map<String,String>), createdAt, updatedAt

Configuration:
  localmind.n8n.base-url: http://localhost:5678
  localmind.n8n.webhook-path: /webhook
  localmind.n8n.timeout: 30s
  localmind.n8n.retry.max-attempts: 3, backoff-ms: 2000
  localmind.n8n.auth.enabled: true, type: basic, username: ${N8N_USERNAME}, password: ${N8N_PASSWORD}

Workflow examples:
  Auto-summary on document indexed: DOCUMENT_INDEXED -> get doc -> POST /api/v1/agents/execute (BUSINESS agent) -> save summary -> email user
  Auto-classify email: NEW_FILE (.eml) -> upload -> await DOCUMENT_INDEXED -> POST /api/v1/agents/execute (classify) -> apply tag -> move file
  Weekly report: SCHEDULED (Fri 17:00) -> POST /api/v1/agents/execute (BUSINESS agent weekly report) -> format HTML -> email

Knowledge Graph relevance:
  New graph events (GRAPH_NODE_CREATED, GRAPH_EDGE_ADDED, GRAPH_WEIGHT_UPDATED) are not yet in the AutomationEvent enum
  Enterprise vertical (ENT-04) and Phase 5 weight reinforcement events may require extending AutomationEvent
  n8n callbacks to /api/v1/graph-rag/query would be a natural enterprise automation pattern (not yet defined)

## Topic: User Interface — Functional Specification

source: documentazione/03-analisi-funzionale/05-interfaccia-utente.md

Technology stack:
  Framework: Angular 21
  Language: TypeScript (strict mode)
  Architecture: Standalone components (no NgModules)
  State management: Angular Signals
  Styling: SCSS with custom design system
  HTTP: Angular HttpClient
  Routing: Angular Router with lazy loading
  Build: Angular CLI / esbuild

Layout: two-column (sidebar 260px + content area)
  Sidebar: collapsible to 64px icons, fixed on desktop, overlay on tablet
  Color scheme: #1a1a2e dark sidebar, #e0e0e0 text, #4f46e5 indigo accent
  Content area: #f8f9fa (light) or #121212 (dark mode), 24px padding

Sections:
  Chat: provider+model dropdown in header; message list (user/assistant/loading); citation blocks; agent selector; token counter (advanced only)
  Documents: grid card view with status badges (PENDING=yellow, PROCESSING=blue, INDEXED=green, FAILED=red, ARCHIVED=gray); upload button; document detail with chunk/embedding info; retry/archive/delete actions
  Search: text search bar; result cards with filename, chunk index, similarity score (0.0-1.0), extracted text; score indicator bar; filters (advanced: top_k, threshold, format/date)
  Folders: folder cards with path, recursive flag, enabled flag, last scan time, file/indexed counts; scan-now, edit, remove actions; add-folder dialog
  Settings: LLM provider cards with enable toggle, API key (masked), test connection, default provider selector, fallback chain configuration; advanced: timeout, temperature, max_tokens defaults
  Dashboard: service health cards (MySQL/Qdrant/Ollama/n8n with UP/DOWN/DEGRADED + latency); usage stats (tokens, cost, requests, latency); document counts by status; batch job stats

Interface modes:
  Simple: agent selection only (no technical params), basic upload/search, minimal dashboard
  Advanced: provider/model/temperature/maxTokens selection, RAG config visible, token/latency/cost metrics, log/diagnostic access

Role presets (activate agent + params for role):
  Developer: Tech agent, temp 0.2, max 4096, Advanced mode
  Business: Business agent, temp 0.5, max 4096, Simple mode
  Legal: Legal agent, temp 0.1, max 4096, Simple mode
  Personal: Personal agent, temp 0.7, max 2048, Simple mode

Design principles:
  Accessible: WCAG 2.1 level AA
  Responsive: desktop + tablet (mobile as future objective)
  Component-based: every element is a standalone Angular component

Knowledge Graph relevance:
  Phase 6 (Graph Visualization): new graph-page route and graph-canvas component follow the same standalone component pattern
  Phase 7 (GraphRAG Chat): extends the existing chat section with graph-awareness; streaming SSE pattern already implemented in existing chat
  The Simple/Advanced mode toggle pattern should extend to hide/show graph filter panel in advanced mode
  Role presets could gain a "Knowledge Graph" preset in Phase 6/7

## Topic: Dashboard and Monitoring — Functional Specification

source: documentazione/03-analisi-funzionale/06-dashboard-monitoraggio.md

Backend: REST health endpoint + Spring Boot Actuator
Frontend: Angular Signal-based reactive stat cards with 30s polling

Health endpoint: GET /api/v1/dashboard/health
  Response structure: { status (UP/DOWN/DEGRADED), timestamp, services: { mysql, qdrant, ollama, n8n }, metrics: { totalTokens, totalCostUsd, totalRequests, averageLatencyMs }, documents: { total, indexed, pending, processing, failed, archived }, batchJobs: { completed, failed, running, lastExecution } }

Service monitoring:
  MySQL: SELECT 1 via JDBC, 5s timeout, 30s interval
  Qdrant: GET /health via HTTP, 5s timeout, 30s interval
  Ollama: GET /api/tags via HTTP, 10s timeout, 30s interval
  n8n: GET / via HTTP, 5s timeout, 60s interval

Token metrics aggregation: by provider, model, day (promptTokens, completionTokens, totalTokens)
Cost metrics aggregation: dailyCost, weeklyCost, monthlyCost, totalCost (by provider)
Latency metrics: averageLatencyMs, p50LatencyMs, p95LatencyMs, p99LatencyMs, maxLatencyMs (by provider)
Document metrics: totalDocuments, indexedDocuments, pendingDocuments, processingDocuments, failedDocuments, archivedDocuments, totalChunks
Batch job metrics: completedJobs, failedJobs, runningJobs, lastJobExecution, lastJobDuration

Spring Boot Actuator:
  Exposed endpoints: /actuator/health, /actuator/info, /actuator/metrics, /actuator/metrics/{name}
  Prometheus endpoint (/actuator/prometheus): planned, not yet active

JVM metrics available: jvm.memory.used, jvm.memory.max, jvm.threads.live, jvm.gc.pause, process.cpu.usage, process.uptime
HTTP metrics: http.server.requests, http.server.requests.active
DB pool metrics: hikaricp.connections.active, hikaricp.connections.idle, hikaricp.connections.max

Frontend: Signal-based polling (interval 30s), computed signals derive aggregated values; DashboardComponent uses inject() + switchMap; stat cards: service health (green/red), tokens (blue), cost (orange), documents (green), batch jobs (purple), latency (cyan)

Knowledge Graph relevance:
  Phase 5 / Phase 6: graph-specific metrics (node count, edge count, reconciliation job status, GraphRAG query count, average GraphRAG latency) are not in the current health response schema
  Extending GET /api/v1/dashboard/health to include a "graph" section is needed for Phase 6 frontend
  Phase 5 WeightDecayJob (nightly) and GraphQdrantReconciliationJob (Phase 3) should appear in the batchJobs section

This document describes the post-v1.0 vision as of February 2026, with RICE-scored priority matrix. Many items listed as future targets are now COMPLETATO (Feb 2026). The current development direction (Knowledge Graph engine) supersedes this document for planning purposes.

CRITICAL NOTE — Knowledge Graph technology conflict:
  Section 2.7 proposes Neo4j Community (graph database) + spaCy/LLM NER as the Knowledge Graph implementation.
  This CONFLICTS with the current plan (PROJECT.md Out of Scope: "Database a grafo dedicato (es. Neo4j) — escluso in questo ciclo: si riusa MySQL + Qdrant").
  See INGEST-CONFLICTS.md [WARNING] "Neo4j future-evolution mention".
  IMPORTANT: this is the ONLY Neo4j mention in the ingest set — all 25 new PRDs explicitly REJECT Neo4j and adopt MySQL+Qdrant, i.e. they are consistent with the locked datastore decision.

Architectural evolutions described (for reference):

## PRD VERTICAL CONTEXT (25 ambiti-estensione docs)

Per-domain personas, value proposition, KPIs and key risks. All verticals share the universal
constraints in `constraints.md` (MySQL+Qdrant, no Neo4j; weighted GraphRAG; Ollama default;
PF4J modules; hexagonal). One phase per APPLICATION vertical is intended; the 6 CROSS-CUTTING
domains enrich existing phases 1-7.

### Structural note for the roadmapper (READ FIRST)
The existing ROADMAP collapses ALL verticals into Phase 8 (Consumer) and Phase 9 (Enterprise),
and REQUIREMENTS.md relegates 15 of 19 verticals to v2 as umbrella items AMBIT-01 / AMBIT-02.
The user has DECIDED to promote the 19 application verticals to GRANULAR v1 phases (one phase
per domain, prefixes per requirements.md). Existing CONS-* (Phase 8) and ENT-* (Phase 9)
requirements become the seed/first vertical of each ecosystem; the remaining verticals expand
beyond them. This restructure is surfaced as INGEST-CONFLICTS.md [WARNING] "Roadmap restructure".

### CONSUMER verticals

TUR — Turismo & territorio
source: 15-ambiti-estensione/01-turismo-territorio-it.md
personas: Esploratore, Local explorer, Contributor/curatore, Operatore DMO/Comune, Operatore esperienziale, Sviluppatore
value: community-driven "Wikipedia of places"; explainable hidden-gem discovery via weighted graph; anti-overtourism boost
risks: data licensing (OSM ODbL, Wikidata), cold-start sparsity, geo/temporal query performance on MySQL CTE

EVT — Eventi & spettacoli
source: 15-ambiti-estensione/02-eventi-spettacoli-it.md
